name: NY-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Deeply Democratic district with a D+24 partisan lean
Incumbent Gregory Meeks has a large financial edge ($2.0M on hand) and no meaningful outside opposition
Prediction markets price Meeks near certain to win
No public general-election polling, but none expected in a seat this lopsided
model.rationale: This Queens-based seat leans Democratic by roughly 24 points, and longtime incumbent Gregory Meeks is running again with a dominant fundraising position and no outside spending against him. Markets price his reelection at near certainty, and nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or an unexpected incumbent retirement could put this seat in play, and neither appears on the horizon.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New York's 5th District, covering parts of Queens and Nassau County, is one of the most Democratic seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 24 points toward Democrats. Gregory Meeks, the incumbent since 1998, is seeking another term and holds a substantial financial advantage, with roughly $2 million on hand after raising $1.7 million. Republican challenger George Marsh has no reported fundraising, and outside groups are not engaging in the race.

Prediction markets put Meeks's chances at about 97 percent, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no public polling and no expert raters flagging the race as competitive, the evidence points to an easy incumbent win, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
